rationale.intervention_reconstruction: The hypothesis proposes microalloying to introduce fine grain-boundary precipitates, whereas the paper synthesizes an equimolar WTaTiVZr refractory high-entropy alloy and compares it with pure tungsten. These are fundamentally different kinds of interventions (compositional alloying vs. microalloying for precipitate control).
rationale.condition_agreement: The hypothesis specifies high-temperature tensile testing under fusion-relevant conditions, while the paper uses room-temperature compression, temperature-dependent indentation plastometry up to 500 °C, and room-temperature scratch testing. The testing modes and temperature ranges differ substantially.
rationale.mechanism_agreement: The hypothesis invokes fine grain-boundary precipitates facilitating dynamic recovery and dislocation absorption. The paper attributes strength to solid-solution strengthening and lattice distortion, and plasticity/toughness to valence-electron concentration, dislocation-core modification, and grain-boundary cohesion, without invoking precipitates or dynamic recovery.
rationale.outcome_agreement: Both predict increased plastic strain and fracture toughness relative to a baseline, but the hypothesis predicts this under high-temperature tensile conditions, while the paper demonstrates it under room-temperature compression, indentation, and scratch testing. The property and direction are broadly similar, but the testing context and specifics differ.
